director.chapterArc: A tense, tactical standoff that escalates into a brutal skirmish and concludes with a devastating realization of vulnerability.
director.restraintNote: Maintain clinical detachment during combat descriptions; let the horror emerge from the precision of movement rather than volume or speed. The emotional weight lies in Rook's admission of error at the end, not the fighting itself.

cues.delivery: Introduce Hoyle with a flat, pleasant tone that masks the threat; she is not shouting but stating facts.
cues.from: She was about fifty-five, small, grey, wearing a good coat that had been mended in three places by three different people. She had a short-handled billhook through her belt and she did not put her hand anywhere near it at any point in the next quarter of an hour.
cues.through: "Stop there, please," she said, at about fifteen feet. "That's near enough for both of us and I'd rather not do the dance."
cues.reason: Establishing the antagonist's deceptive calm before the tension rises.

cues.delivery: Shift to Toren's internal observation; a moment of realization where he recognizes the danger in Hoyle's speech patterns.
cues.from: Toren stood on a brick in a road and discovered that he was doing exactly what he had been told for twenty days not to do.
cues.through: He will talk. Every single word out of his mouth in those eight feet is a hand pushing you somewhere.
cues.reason: Internal pivot from external action to psychological assessment.

cues.delivery: Narrate the shift in Hoyle's demeanor; the pleasantness drops away like paint to reveal cold calculation.
cues.from: And Toren, standing on a brick twelve feet away with his hands open at his sides, watched a woman of fifty-five come off the road she had been standing on for a quarter of an hour.
cues.through: "That's not an answer, and you knew it wasn't when you gave it to me." She stepped back one pace, which put her at nine feet, which Toren understood afterward had been the whole conversation ending. "Go and ask your old woman. Come back and tell me. And when you come back, be somebody who has decided, because I have eight people on this platform who have been very patient for five days and I am running out of ways to describe you to them."
cues.reason: The moment the conversation turns from negotiation to confrontation.

cues.delivery: Rook's voice remains flat and factual; he is stating a grim probability without emotional coloring.
cues.from: "There's no rest that's a fact. There's what I think, and what I think is worth exactly what any of you decide it's worth." Rook's voice did not change by one degree. "She'd take you. She'd get you there. She would very likely get you there alive, and I'd put it at better than even. And somewhere between here and Meridian somebody would say a thing in front of you, or you'd see a thing in a cart, and then there would be an old woman and two children who had been inside a company's arrangements for five days.
cues.through: "And that's a record," said Rook. "That's the only kind they've never been able to buy."
cues.reason: Maintaining the 'bill-reading' cadence for high-stakes information.

cues.delivery: A slow, observational scan of the abandoned platform; emphasize the eerie order and silence.
cues.from: Here is what it is like to walk into a place that other people have just left.
cues.through: And on the inside of the engine house doorway, out of the weather, there was a tally chalked up on the brick: five gates, five dates, and a running figure at the bottom that Toren could not make anything of.
cues.reason: Building atmosphere through stillness before the action resumes.

cues.delivery: Staccato pacing for Rook's movement; describe the violence as a series of precise mechanical actions rather than chaotic noise.
cues.from: Rook went at it and he went at it fast.
cues.through: There was no crash and nothing flashed. A man going at speed simply stopped, three feet short of a woman standing with her palms turned down, the way a boot stops in thick mud, and every bit of what he had put into it went somewhere and did not come back.
cues.reason: Combat must feel clinical and immediate, not heroic or melodramatic.

cues.delivery: Rook's retreat is a tactical necessity; his voice should be sharp but not panicked.
cues.from: And he saw Rook go backward out of the arch. On his feet, facing them, giving ground one pace at a time, down the slope of the hump, with the blade up and his left arm low and bent — and Toren, who had watched that man for thirty-three days and had never once seen him give a single inch of anything to anybody, understood with total clarity that this was not a trick.
cues.through: "Back!" Rook said. "Cart. Now. Turn it and go."
cues.reason: Clarifying the shift from offense to defense.

cues.delivery: Rapid-fire delivery for Milo's throw and Toren's hook; the action is fast but described with precise detail.
cues.through: He never made any sound at all.
cues.reason: Capturing the split-second nature of the combat without rushing the narration.

cues.delivery: A quiet observation of Cinder Company carrying their dead; the horror is in what they do calmly.
cues.from: Four people were coming down it at a walk. Not at them. Off to the west side, down the rip-rap, to the two men lying at the bottom of it, and they went into the water up to their thighs and they got the first one up under the arms and carried him.
cues.reason: Contrast between the violence and the mundane aftermath.

cues.delivery: Rook's admission of error; delivered with a weary flatness that carries the weight of his failure.
cues.from: Rook looked out at the water.
cues.reason: The emotional climax is Rook's vulnerability, not the fighting.

pauses.after: "Stop there, please," she said, at about fifteen feet. "That's near enough for both of us and I'd rather not do the dance."
pauses.reason: Speaker reset and dramatic landing on Hoyle's command to stop.
Emphasis on the specific location that defines the boundary of safety.
Preparation for Rook's dangerous question about the paybook.
Major emotional landing; the shift in power dynamic after Rook asks about the paybook.

pauses.after: The platform was empty. The fire was smoking on its own. The washing was still on the line.
pauses.reason: Speaker reset and scene transition to the empty platform observation.
Isolating the critical tactical detail Wyck is recalling.

pauses.after: "It's four inches narrower than he said," Wyck said.
pauses.reason: Emotional landing on Wyck's realization that the door is better than expected; a moment of quiet relief in tension.
Completed thought; Toren's visceral reaction to seeing Marta Faust again.

pauses.after: That was the whole of it. Half a second, and a man with his hands on his own face.
pauses.reason: Light continuation after the description of Milo's throw; maintaining momentum into the next action beat.
Emphasis on the brevity of Milo's action and its impact.

pauses.after: He never made any sound at all.
pauses.reason: Speaker reset and dramatic landing on the silence following Lask's fall.

pauses.after: Toren watched Cinder Company carry their own dead man four hundred yards up a bank in the last of the light, and found that his hands had started, and could not make them stop.
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing; Toren's reaction to seeing Cinder Company carry their dead man calmly.

pauses.after: "You aimed at the eye and you got the bone above it, at thirty feet, backhand, moving, in bad light." Rook looked at him. "That's the best thing anybody did on this bank today and I want it said out loud in front of everybody before anyone goes to sleep."
pauses.reason: Speaker reset and dramatic landing on Rook's praise for Milo's shot.
Major emotional landing; the summary of costs and Rook's physical state.
